roles.format_summary: JSON object with structured data about HTTP requests and login attempts

roles.role: The IP address of the client making the request
A unique identifier for each HTTP request, used to correlate logs between clients and servers in transactions
The HTTP method used (e.g., GET, POST)
The resource path requested by the client
The version of the HTTP protocol used (e.g., HTTP/1.1)
The user agent header as sent by the client, indicating the software making the request
The result code the server answered with (200 for a login, 403 for a refused one)
The number of bytes in the response content
The time when the log entry was created, in epoch seconds
The component name of the emitting logger
How serious the entry is (e.g., INFO, WARNING)

unresolved.reason: The role text suggests 'Timestamp of the log entry in seconds since the epoch', but ECS has 'event.created' which is a timestamp with timezone info. The unit of the source key is not specified, so it could be either.
The role text mentions 'Time taken to respond in seconds', but ECS has 'event.duration' which is in nanoseconds. There is no direct conversion available in the IR.
The role text specifies 'Indicator if the response was served from cache (1 for yes, 0 for no)', but ECS has 'dns.header_flags' which is a string. There is no direct mapping available.

The role text states 'Size of the DNS response in bytes', but ECS has 'network.bytes' which represents total bytes transferred in both directions. This field may not be suitable for size of a single response.
